question.problem:
Let $V=C[-\frac{\pi }{2},0],$ the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[-\frac{\pi }{2},0].$ Find $⟨5{cos}^{4}⁡t,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ if the inner product on $V$ is defined as

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$
question.worked_solution:
We need to evaluate

$$
⟨5{cos}^{4}⁡t,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}5{cos}^{4}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t.
$$

We can evaluate this integral using the substitution $u=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,$ $\text{d}u=-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}5{cos}^{4}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =-5{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}{cos}^{4}⁡t\,(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-5{\int }_{0}^{1}{u}^{4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-5\cdot {\frac{{u}^{5}}{5}|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-(1)^{5}+(0)^{5} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$
